page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Pulvinus — definition
lines: A swollen leaf base is called a pulvinus.
steps.why: The definition is one line - the leaf BASE (the part joining the stem) is swollen.
common_mistakes: Writing swollen petiole. The pulvinus is the swollen leaf BASE, not the whole stalk.
steps.memory_tip: Pulvinus - a pillow at the base of the leaf.
steps.margin_note: One sentence is the full first mark.

steps.label: The family

lines.text: It is found in members of Fabaceae

steps.why: The family name is the second mark; Fabaceae is the accepted modern name and Leguminosae the older one. The book prints 'Leguminoceae', a misspelling.
common_mistakes: Misspelling the family as Leguminoceae (the book's spelling). Write Fabaceae or Leguminosae.
steps.memory_tip: Pulvinus and pea family go together - Fabaceae.
steps.margin_note: Either family name earns the mark; spell it correctly.
